records.title: Help shoppers find the genuine online store
records.lesson: Make legitimate order tracking and scam reporting easy to find from the retailer’s official website.

timeline.summary: UK guidance explains how to recognise fraudulent shops and use official routes to reach retailers.

records.title: Next responds to a reported supplier incident
records.exposure: The retailer said it had found no evidence that customer personal data was affected at the time of its statement. The wider scope was still being investigated.
records.lesson: Agree who verifies impact and who communicates with customers when an incident is reported by a supplier.

timeline.summary: The Register reported a breach at an online supplier to Next and quoted the retailer’s assessment. The public report did not establish an incident in Next’s own systems.

records.title: Cleverbridge discloses copying of data from its platform
records.impact: Cleverbridge reported temporarily taking affected systems offline and restoring them on 4 November.
records.exposure: Cleverbridge confirmed copying of some personal data, including some payment card information.
records.lesson: Ask payment providers which card data they retain and how they notify affected customers.

timeline.summary: The company dates the start of customer notifications to 20 November and reports that data was copied from its platform.
A Retail Watch evidence review noted that the company FAQ identified card security codes among the data involved in some cases.

records.title: McDonald’s Japan discloses unauthorised access to app data
records.exposure: The company confirmed access to some customer-related app data, including purchase histories. Copying was not established in the notice.
records.lesson: Review how retail apps separate customer information and restrict access to purchase history.

timeline.summary: The company confirmed that a third party accessed some customer-related information in its official app database. This is international sector intelligence.
